strategies.name: Detection Strategy for Masquerading via Account Name Similarity

analytics.name: Analytic 1077
analytics.guidance: Detects adversary behavior where a newly created or renamed user account closely resembles existing service or administrator accounts to blend in and avoid detection. Common patterns include prefix/suffix modifications, homoglyphs, or use of names like 'admin1', 'adm1n', or 'backup_help'.

tuning.description: Defines how close in Levenshtein or visual distance an account name must be to a legitimate one to raise an alert.
Set of known legitimate accounts to compare new account names against.
Period within which anomalous account creation or renaming is evaluated in relation to discovery or deletion activity.

log_sources.name: windows:osquery
log_sources.channel: User enumeration with creation/last modified timestamps

analytics.name: Analytic 1078
analytics.guidance: Detects creation or renaming of accounts with names that closely match known service, root, or admin accounts. Behavior often follows account discovery or deletion, attempting to blend into system activity logs using trusted name conventions.

tuning.description: Whitelist of legitimate service accounts used for validation.
Edit distance sensitivity between created account and existing account names.
Whether to flag account creation events triggered from suspicious scripts or shell histories.

log_sources.name: auditd:SYSCALL
log_sources.channel: usermod, or account rename system calls

analytics.name: Analytic 1079
analytics.guidance: Detects adversary creation of cloud or IdP accounts whose names resemble existing privileged or service accounts. May indicate preparation for privilege escalation or defense evasion.

tuning.description: Whether created users have privileged or scoped roles assigned at creation.
Regex patterns or heuristics for detecting suspicious naming conventions (e.g., helpdesk_support_, root-admin).

analytics.name: Analytic 1080
analytics.guidance: Monitors for the creation of accounts inside containers using names that resemble legitimate orchestrator or backup identities to mask adversary persistence.

tuning.description: Limit detection to containers with persistent volumes or specific workloads
Custom list of commonly abused names to blend into container environments (e.g., kubelet, cronjob_sync)
